newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania May inflation forecast cut to 4.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Romania May inflation forecast cut to 4.5 percent.

text.p: Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea on Tuesday revised the forecast for May inflation down to 4.5 percent from his previous estimate of six percent.
Ciorbea gave no reason for the more optimistic forecast, announced during an address to parliament seeking support for his centrist government's four-month-old programme of reforms.
The two chambers, dominated by centrists elected last November, are certain to defeat a no confidence motion to be submitted this week by the leftist opposition.
The prime minister told reporters last week that May inflation would stand at six percent and revised upward to 110 percent from 89.5 percent his year-on-year forecast for 1997.
Analysts said even the new year-on-year figure of 110 percent was unrealistic in view of big price rises since the beginning of the year.
The May figure is certain to be affected by a fivefold increase in the price of heating and domestic natural gas.

Monthly inflation slowed to 6.9 percent in April from March's record 30.7 percent. Consumer prices rose 89.5 percent in April from last December after the government introduced steep price increases for staples, petrol and utilities.
